title: Closing Out and Settling a Keyturn Trip Booking
content:
A trip starts only once the vehicle has actually changed hands, and the start reading of the odometer and of the fuel level is taken at that moment; a reservation whose start reading is missing cannot later be settled on estimates.

The trip may be closed out only while the reservation is in progress or already completed, which is what makes an early return a completion rather than a cancellation.

Returning the vehicle early closes the trip on the day it comes back; where the plan credits early returns, the unused whole days are credited at the plan's early return percentage of the locked daily rate, and where the plan does not, nothing is credited however much time is left.

Settlement is performed once every end-of-trip line that can arise has been posted or ruled out: the mileage settlement, the fuel settlement, any late return, and any cleaning, smoking or pet charge the host has evidenced. Settling a reservation with an end-of-trip line still outstanding is not permitted, because the settled state is what releases the host's money.

Where the reservation carries a Keyturn Business Traveler Protection election, settlement waits until that protection election has itself been completed, since the corporate account is billed as one document covering the trip and its protection together.

Tolls and citations reaching the marketplace after settlement are passed on to the guest with the plan's administration fee added, posted after settlement against the reservation they arose on rather than opening a new one.

A reservation that reaches the settled state is never reopened; a correction after settlement is made as a reversal against the line that was wrong.

### The two conditions, and what settles them

**Closing the trip out.** The reservation must stand in the in-progress or completed state. It is read from the reservation's own record — its status and the date the guest actually took the vehicle — before the trip is closed out, correlated by the reservation's reference number, and it is the system record rather than either party's account that settles it. A reservation in progress that is closed out is completed, not cancelled, which is why an early return is a completion.

**Closing the billing.** Every end-of-trip line that can arise must have been posted or ruled out. It is read from the priced lines already standing against the reservation, by their kind and by the point in the trip they fall due at, correlated by the reservation's reference number and established before the reservation is settled.

### The end-of-trip lines that must be settled first

| Line | Ruled out where |
|---|---|
| The mileage settlement | No overage arises on the reservation. |
| The fuel settlement | No shortfall beyond the tolerance arises. |
| A late return | The vehicle was not returned late. |
| A cleaning, smoking or pet charge | The host has evidenced none. |

### An early return

*Hypothetical.* A reservation runs 10 reserved days and the vehicle comes back after 6, on a plan whose early return credit is 50 per cent of the locked daily rate. The trip closes on the day the vehicle comes back. The unused whole days are 4, and each is credited at 50 per cent of the locked daily rate. On a plan that does not credit early returns, nothing is credited, however many whole days are left.

### After the reservation is settled

A settled reservation is never reopened. A toll or a citation that reaches the marketplace afterwards is posted against that same reservation, with the plan's administration fee added, rather than opening a new one; and a correction to a line that was wrong is made as a reversal against that line.
